newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi president's son's paper assails Albright.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi president's son's paper assails Albright.

text.p: Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel ridiculed U.S. Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright on Tuesday and described her performance when submitting a report to the Congress last week as stupid.

"Albright has become a laughing stock...With great stupidity she read her forged report dictated by the American administration in a dramatic way," said the paper owned by President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday.
Babel condemned U.S. foreign policy, calling it inhumane.

Albright has been the target of scathing criticism by Iraq during her term as the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations. Mad woman, a snake and scorpion were among names given to her by official Iraqi media.
Iraq also blamed her for Washington's tough stand on sanctions imposed on Baghdad for invading Kuwait in 1990.
In 1991 the United States led the Gulf War against Iraq, driving its troops out of Kuwait.
"The time span of American arrogance is short and Iraq's land, people and leadership will stay," the paper said.
